newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Acquisition-hungry Persetel eyes more buys.
newsitem.headline: Acquisition-hungry Persetel eyes more buys.

text.p: Persetel Holdings Ltd, which on Monday announced it would buy a controlling stake in German firm Telemation AG, plans further acquisitions this year continuing a trend started in 1996, chairman Roux Marnitz said.
"We have said before that we will be looking at one or two other acquisitions before the end of the year," Marnitz told Reuters on Monday.
He would, however, not provide any details saying only that cautionary announcements would be released well in advance of any purchases.

The South African information technology business on Monday said it would buy a 70 percent stake in Telemation for an undisclosed sum. Payment would be made through the issue of 70-million Persetel shares.
Marnitz would not reveal the purchase price saying Persetel had an agreement with the vendor not to disclose it.
"The shares (for payment) were placed a little while ago, so they price will be at a bit of a discount to where shares were today and on Friday," Marnitz said.
By the close on Monday shares on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange had lost 155 cents or almost four percent of their value to 37.50, toppling off a record close on Friday of 39.05.
Dealers blamed the weakness on concerns the firm had overpaid for the German purchase.
They said profits were also being taken by investors following announcement of the deal.

Persetel shares have rocketed almost 400 percent since the beginning of last year on the back of an 80 percent surge in attributable income in the year to end May, 1996 and the acquisition of numerous data businesses last year.
Results for the six months to end November, 1996 will be released in the first week of February, Marnitz said.
